column1: # EN 926-2 flight test reports — what a certificate actually measures
# Source: para-test.com, Air Turquoise flight test reports
# Retrieved: 2026-09-21
# measure: as-published
# A certificate is mostly QUALITATIVE: A/B ratings and phrases like "dive
# forward 0 to 30 degrees" or "spontaneous in less than 3 s". It is a record
# of how a wing behaved when a test pilot provoked it, not a set of numbers.
# Four things in it ARE quantitative, and they are what this file holds:
#   totalWeightKg      the all-up weight each test was flown at. Every wing is
#                      flown twice, at the low and high end of its certified
#                      range, which is why there are two rows per size.
#   harnessToRisersCm  measured on the harness used for that test
#   riserSeparationCm  distance between the karabiners
#   speed bounds       trim speed, minimum speed and the control range, given
#                      as THRESHOLDS rather than values: "more than 30 km/h",
#                      "less than 25 km/h", "larger than 10 km/h"
# The speed fields are bounds a model must satisfy, not figures to fit to.
# There is no polar here: no sink rate, no glide ratio, no speed at any given
# brake position.
